Compiled successfully. I wrote `FastTimeZoneAgentTest` under `tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/`, covering all three documented methods:

- **`getGmtTimeZone()`** — zero raw offset, consistency across calls.
- **`getGmtTimeZone(String)`** — recognized literals (`Z`, `UTC`), inputs lacking a digit group that still match with zero offset (`""`, `"+"`, `"-"`, `"GMT"`), parsed numeric offsets (single/double-digit hours, colon-separated minutes, negative signs, `GMT` prefix), the documented boundary of validity (`+23:59`/`-23:59`), out-of-range rejections (`≥24` hours, `≥60` minutes, both), and regex-failure rejections (non-matching letters, trailing garbage).
- **`getTimeZone(String)`** — GMT-custom-id recognition (`Z`, `UTC`, signed offsets, `GMT` prefix) and Olson-id fallback (valid zone IDs preserving their offset/ID, plus the JDK-documented fallback to `"GMT"` for an unrecognized zone id).

All assertions are grounded in the javadoc contract in `api/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastTimeZone.html` (plus the well-documented JDK `TimeZone.getTimeZone` fallback behavior), not internal implementation guesses.
